clue.text: Acted like a vandal and was dismissed

definitions.meaning: to plunder or lay waste to a town, as the Vandals did Rome
was fired from a job

explanation.surface: A worker who smashed things up and lost their job for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Plundered a place is one sense, and being fired from employment is the other.

clue.text: Press men in China

definitions.meaning: to force men into service at sea, kidnapping them as crew
a great port city located in China

explanation.surface: Journalists reporting from the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press men' looks like journalists, but it is a verb phrase: to press-gang men.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap sailors for a crew is named after the Chinese port, which is also the city itself.

clue.text: Gets up, but it involves a scramble

indicators.note: the word that follows is to be jumbled, since it involves a scramble of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a slope, but has to scramble to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scramble' is both the fodder and, in the surface, a climb, which suits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbs awkwardly upward, a synonym of scrambling up a slope.

clue.text: Around midday set out the food

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go around the middle letter, so they surround it
set out suggests the letters are laid out differently, so rearrange them

parts.note: the middle letter of the word day is A

explanation.surface: Laying out a meal at about noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to ETS, and 'Around' puts that around A, the middle of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for grub or things to munch.

clue.text: Nuts are found in them, and bolts

definitions.meaning: coal nuts, small lumps of coal, are kept in coal buckets by the fire
runs off hurriedly

explanation.surface: A hardware drawer of nuts and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' and 'bolts' pair up as hardware; here nuts are small lumps of coal and bolts means dashes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal buckets hold coal nuts; and to hurry off with short quick steps is to bolt.

clue.text: Bringing into force

parts.note: read as bringing people into the armed forces by compulsory call-up, rather than making a law effective

explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory enlistment for military service brings civilians into the armed forces.

clue.text: Egotistical dedication for a book

definitions.meaning: a dedication addressed to the writer personally, not to anyone else
a large heavy volume

explanation.surface: A vain author dedicates a volume to themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A dedication to oneself reads 'to me', and a weighty volume is the other sense.

clue.text: Forms with no head girls

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off, the word losing its head

parts.note: school forms are classes

explanation.surface: School forms left without a head teacher, full of girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' removes the first letter C from CLASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Young women, a Scottish and northern word for girls.

clue.text: Last of the late-comers gets rot ten seat

indicators.note: the final letter of the word late-comers is taken

parts.note: rotten, as an egg, is addle (the newspaper prints it split as 'rot ten')

explanation.surface: Latecomers end up with a broken-down seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last of' takes S from 'late-comers'; ADDLE means gone bad, like an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to sit on, as a rider's seat on a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Stays will alter a waist

indicators.note: the letters of a waist are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A corset will change the shape of a waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a corset, which does alter a waist; it is the verb, remains or waits for.
explanation.definitionFit: Waits for or is in store, a near synonym of stays put for.

clue.text: Girl thought to be like Queen Victoria

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
mused means pondered

explanation.surface: A girl believed to resemble the old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is reputed to have said 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria's famous remark shows her as not entertained.

clue.text: Unreliable combination of opposites

definitions.meaning: irresponsible, not to be trusted
the phrase joins two words of opposite sense, fixed and slack

explanation.surface: A mix of contradictions makes for an untrustworthy thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To play it this way is to behave irresponsibly; the phrase joins firm with slack, two contrary words.

clue.text: Note retreat of W.African tribe to desert

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: retreat means go back, so the tribe's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Ibo are a people of Nigeria

explanation.surface: A West African tribe pulls back into the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat of' turns IBO round to OBI.
explanation.definitionFit: The great desert of Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: A month in advance

definitions.meaning: the third month of the year
to walk forward in step, as soldiers

explanation.surface: A deadline set a month ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The third calendar month, and to proceed as troops on the move.

clue.text: Inventor of the telephone or part of it

definitions.meaning: the Scottish-born inventor Alexander Graham, who patented it in 1876
the ringer in an old telephone

explanation.surface: Asking who invented the phone, or one of its components.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell patented the phone, whose ringer gives the second sense.

clue.text: Record membership

parts.note: read as writing one's name on a register to join, not a record-breaking number of members

explanation.definitionFit: To sign up and be entered on a roll of members.

clue.text: Open a fresh page

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of page are rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning to a fresh page of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges PAGE into GAPE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Wide open, as a mouth hanging in astonishment.

clue.text: Family ties for the mother's boy

definitions.text: Family ties for the mother's boy

parts.words: Family ties for the mother's boy
parts.note: the ties of a pinafore a mother wears, to which a dependent son is said to be tied

explanation.definitionFit: Being 'tied to one's mother's' pinafore cords is the idiom for a son's dependence.

clue.text: Turn a wench into a winch

parts.note: to wind is to turn a handle
a wench is a lass

explanation.surface: Transforming a serving girl into a lifting machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is only a link here, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-cranked hoisting drum, a type of hoist.

clue.text: See great changes in economy travel

indicators.note: the letters of see great undergo changes into a new order

explanation.surface: Big changes in budget travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SEE and GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest class of passenger accommodation on a ship.

clue.text: Indicate the spot for country meeting

parts.note: to point to something is to indicate it
a point is a particular spot or place

explanation.surface: Showing where a rural gathering is held.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an amateur steeplechase horse race run across country, a British rural sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural steeplechase for amateur riders on hunters; and to direct someone to the exact place.

clue.text: Making jokes with no beginning, purely visual

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped, the word losing its beginning

parts.note: jocular means joking

explanation.surface: Comedy without words, all sight gags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no beginning' drops J from JOCULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the eye, hence concerned only with sight.

clue.text: Beats making money!

definitions.meaning: hits repeatedly
British currency units

explanation.surface: Drumming up cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammers or batters, and the units of sterling.

clue.text: Short cut taken when hunting

definitions.meaning: a close-cropped haircut
a riding whip carried on the hunt

explanation.surface: A quick route through the fields during the hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short haircut, and the riding whip a hunter carries.

clue.text: A tax return to distribute

indicators.note: return means come back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A tax return that shares money out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TOLL into LLOT after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To share out or apportion.

clue.text: Vain and averse to work

definitions.meaning: futile or to no purpose, as empty threats
lazy

explanation.surface: A conceited, lazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile or empty, as an empty boast; and lazy.

clue.text: Poe's house-owner is heartless employer

indicators.note: the middle letter, the heart of the word, is taken away

parts.note: Roderick Usher of Poe's 'The Fall of the House of Usher'

explanation.surface: A landlord in a Poe tale is a cruel boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes H, the middle letter of USHER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who employs, that is uses, something.

clue.text: Famous ship is short of freight

indicators.note: the word is cut short by one letter, here its first

parts.note: cargo is freight

explanation.surface: A celebrated vessel lacking a load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' takes C off CARGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason's vessel, carrying the Argonauts in Greek myth.

clue.text: Cricketer yearns to be a spinner

parts.note: longs means yearns
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A cricketer longs to be a spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: A long stop is a fielding position directly behind the wicketkeeper in cricket; 'spinner' suggests a spin bowler but is a spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: A fielder placed far behind the wicketkeeper, named after that position.

clue.text: A jolly girl for the Fleet

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl going down to the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like cheerful but is slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: A great naval force, as the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Kept quiet

definitions.meaning: held back, booked
reticent, shy

explanation.surface: Kept silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Set aside, as a booked table; and reticent in manner.

clue.text: Mix us some pudding

indicators.note: the letters of us some are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Whip up a dessert for us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix' rearranges US and SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert.
